Tottenham Secure Third Successive Premier League Win After Defeating 10-Man Crystal Palace

Tottenham Hotspur have claimed three consecutive Premier League victories for the first time in nearly 21 months following a home win against Crystal Palace.

Match and Statistical Overview

Crystal Palace were reduced to 10 players early in the match after striker Jean-Philippe Mateta received a red card for a challenge on Micky van de Ven in the 13th minute. Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke scored to secure the result for Tottenham, building on earlier league wins against Coventry City and Chelsea.

According to published match statistics:

  • Tottenham registered 34 shots compared to two for Crystal Palace.
  • Spurs finished the match with 79.4% possession.
  • Crystal Palace remain in the relegation zone with two wins from nine league fixtures under head coach Pierre Sage.

Manager and Player Reactions

Tottenham head coach Roberto de Zerbi highlighted the team's concentration and work rate following the victory. Speaking to BBC Sport, De Zerbi urged patience regarding high-profile summer acquisitions Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, both of whom featured in the starting lineup.

"The passion we showed - we didn't lose the focus, the concentration," De Zerbi told BBC Sport's Match Of The Day. He added that the squad must remain ambitious while acknowledging recent struggles over previous seasons.

Dejan Kulusevski also made a substitute appearance following a long injury absence, forcing a save from Crystal Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson.
